title: The 10 Best Corded Jigsaws
subtitle: Wired jigsaws ranked from live Amazon data — curves, cutouts, and bevels for the least money, no battery to run down.
intro: A jigsaw is the tool for curves, circles, and cutouts that a straight-cutting saw can't touch, and a corded one gives you steady power for as long as the cut takes. The best-sellers here run 4.5 to 7 amps and cost less than a single pro battery. What separates them is the stuff you use every day: variable speed, orbital settings for faster cuts, and whether you can swap blades without hunting for a wrench. This list covers 10 corded jigsaws from budget kits to pro top-handles.

avoid.name: Extbtfor 350W Corded Jig Saw, 0-3000 RPM, 45° Bevel
avoid.flag: 3.5 A motor, about half the field
avoid.verdict: It saves about $7 over the DEKOPRO and gives up a lot of motor to do it: 350 watts and 3.5 amps by its own listing, well below every saw above.
reasons: The listing rates the motor at 350 watts and 3.5 amps. Most picks above run 5 to 7 amps, and even the 4.5-amp BLACK+DECKER BDEJS300C has more.
A motor that small bogs down in hardwood and thick stock; the listing itself pitches it at small woodworking and DIY projects.
It gives the stroke as 20 mm, "approximately 1 1/14 inch". 20 mm is about 0.8 inch, so the listing's own conversion is wrong.
No orbital action is listed, so it can't speed up rough cuts the way the 4-position orbital saws above can.
For $29.99 the DEKOPRO adds 4 orbital settings, a parallel guide and a much larger review history.

buyers_guide.q: What is orbital action, and do I need it?
buyers_guide.a: Orbital action swings the blade forward into the cut on the upstroke instead of just moving straight up and down. Higher orbital settings cut faster and rougher, which is great for ripping through softwood; turn it off for slow, clean cuts in hardwood, metal, or finish work. Most jigsaws here offer four settings so you can match the material.

buyers_guide.q: How many amps do I need?
buyers_guide.a: 5 amps handles plywood, trim, and general DIY cutting. 6 to 6.5 amps is the sweet spot for most work, giving you power without bogging down in thicker or harder stock. 7 amps, like the Bosch JS470E, is for frequent or heavy cutting where you don't want the motor to slow under load.

buyers_guide.q: What does tool-free blade change mean?
buyers_guide.a: A tool-free clamp lets you pop a blade in or out by hand or with a lever, no wrench or hex key needed. It sounds minor until you change blades ten times in a project. The DEWALT, both Bosch tools, Makita, SKIL, DEKOPRO, WORKPRO, and BLACK+DECKER BDEJS300C have it; the BLACK+DECKER BDEJS600C and CRAFTSMAN need a small tool.

T-shank (tang) blades are the modern standard and snap into tool-free clamps, with by far the widest selection at any store. U-shank is the older style with a slot. Every tool on this list takes T-shank blades, so buy those and you'll never hunt for a match.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need variable speed and bevel cuts?
buyers_guide.a: Variable speed lets you slow down for metal, laminate, and tight curves and speed up for straight cuts in wood, so it's worth having — every pick here includes it. A bevel base tilts the shoe up to 45 degrees for angled cuts; the WORKPRO tilts both directions, the rest go one way to 45.

A corded jigsaw gives constant power for long or heavy cuts and costs far less, with no battery to buy or recharge. Cordless is worth it only if you need to cut where a cord can't reach or you're already on a battery platform.
